questions.q: What does the `foundry-rs/foundry-toolchain` GitHub Action do?
options: Deploys contracts automatically to mainnet
Installs Foundry on the CI runner so forge/cast commands can be used in later steps
Runs Slither and Mythril automatically
Replaces the need for a checkout step
questions.explain: foundry-toolchain is the official action that installs the Foundry toolchain (forge, cast, anvil) on a GitHub Actions runner.

questions.q: Why does `submodules: recursive` matter specifically for a Foundry project's checkout step?
options: It's required by all GitHub Actions workflows regardless of language
Foundry dependencies like OpenZeppelin and forge-std are usually installed as git submodules, not via an npm-style package manager
It speeds up the Solidity compiler
It's only needed for Hardhat projects, not Foundry
questions.explain: Without recursive submodule checkout, the build fails on missing imports, since Foundry projects typically manage dependencies as git submodules.

questions.q: What does `forge fmt --check` do differently from plain `forge fmt`?
options: It auto-fixes formatting and commits the change
It fails the build on unformatted code without rewriting any files
It only checks test files, not contracts
It disables formatting checks entirely
questions.explain: --check reports a failure on unformatted code instead of rewriting it, which is what you want in CI so the tested branch isn't silently modified.

questions.q: What problem does `forge build --sizes` catch before a deploy script ever runs?
options: Unused imports
A contract that has crept past the 24KB EIP-170 bytecode size limit
Missing NatSpec comments
Incorrect compiler version
questions.explain: forge build --sizes reports each contract's bytecode size, catching an over-the-limit contract in CI instead of failing at actual deploy time.

questions.q: In the GitHub Actions job summary screenshot shown in this lesson, what information is displayed alongside the run's Success status?
options: The contract's gas report only
The trigger event and the total duration of the run
The Etherscan verification link
The Slither findings count
questions.explain: The job summary page shows how the run was triggered, its pass/fail status, and total duration — a real GitHub Actions UI screenshot confirmed in this lesson.
